title: Wood Ash Fertilisation and Heavy Metal Dynamics in Boreal and Temperate Forest Soils: A Systematic Review of Short- and Long-Term Evidence
content: Wood ash returns base cations to forest soil, but also brings heavy metals. This systematic review assessed the impact of applying ash at operational rates on the content, mobility and leaching of heavy metals in soil in temperate and boreal forest soils in Europe and North America. Of 99 studies selected, 15 included both an ash treatment and measurements of metals. Ash application has been shown to raise pH in the organic horizon by 0.5 to 1.6 units and to increase base saturation. Cadmium, zinc, copper, nickel and chromium were shown to accumulate in the forest floor. However, no studies reported metal accumulation in soil solution at a depth of 50 cm after intervals of up to seventeen years, and no studies reported on groundwater. Above approximately 9 t ha-1, soil solution cadmium, aluminium mobilisation and soil pH dropping below that of the control occurred concurrently after the fourth year, indicating a threshold and the depletion of ash alkalinity through nitrification. Using ash to retain rather than remove heavy metals such as cadmium is problematic, as ash applications can represent several years of atmospheric deposition. Moreover, cadmium remains in a pool highly dependent on pH, C/N balance and an unregulated retention period.
